data.long_meaning: Anesia is derived from the Greek word 'anesis,' meaning 'grace, kindness, and mercy.' historical_references.reference: Anesia was an early Christian martyr in Sardinia, Italy. She is said to have been a young girl who was persecuted for her faith during the Diocletian persecution (AD 303-311). According to legend, she was burned at the stake and her body was thrown into the sea, but it was said to have floated and not decomposed. Therefore, the local people venerated her as a saint.

Her relics were later discovered and brought to Thessalonica, where she is now venerated as a patron saint of the city.
